High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:102025
(Sl.No. 44)
Court No. - 81

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5740 of 2024
Applicant :- Mehraj Ali

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Mazhar Ullah,Rizwan Ahmad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1.
Heard Sri Mazhar Ullah, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri S.P. Singh, learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.337 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.
Mainather, District Moradabad, during pendency of the trial.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the complainant-the wife of the applicant has filed the instant F.I.R. on 26.10.2023 alleging therein that she was married to the applicant three years ago and the husband of the complainant is working as an iron contractor in Jodhpur and she used to live with her in-laws.
It has further been alleged that in-laws were demanding dowry of Rs. 5,00,000/- and a car, due to which they regularly used to torture the complainant.

It has been further alleged that brother-in-law of the complainant namely, Rashid used to tease the complainant in the absence of her husband and when she told her mother-in-law about this incident, she said let him do what he wants.

It has further been alleged that on 06.04.2022 at about 01:00 pm the complainant along with Mehraj Ali vs State Of U.P. on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6932046/
1 her children were sleeping then her brother-in-law entered the room and raped her threatening her with knife thereafter, brother-in-law of her husband namely Anis also raped her in collusion with said Rashid.

entities.text: Mehraj Ali vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She had complained about those incident to her husband and mother-in-law, then they asked her to keep mum.
Thus, she informed her parents and went to her maternal house.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as per allegation in the F.I.R. there is no specific allegation against the applicant herein with regard to any demand of dowry made by him and all the incidents which have been narrated have allegedly taken place behind him while he was working in Jodhpur.
Therefore, no prima facie case is made out against him.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that the instant F.I.R. has been lodged after Section 9 application, which has been moved by the applicant on 29.04.2022 and the instant F.I.R. has been lodged on 26.10.2023 with regard to an incident allegedly taken place on 06.04.2022 i.e. after more than one and half years on the basis of a concocted story.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the applicant is innocent and he has criminal history of two other cases, which has been explained in para-19 of the instant application and in both the cases the applicant has already been granted bail by trial court and in case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
5.

Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that all the incidents that took place with the complainant have taken place in the absence of the applicant.

6. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and antecedents and very limited involvement of the applicant, he is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case, in view of the judgment of the the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
7.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Let the applicant-Mehraj Ali be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions, which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable (ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence (iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned.
